decks.name: LeetCode #1046 - Last Stone Weight
decks.description: Simulate stone smashing game to find weight of last remaining stone

cards.question: Last Stone Weight: You are given an array of integers stones where stones[i] is the weight of the ith stone. We are playing a game with the stones. On each turn, we choose the heaviest two stones and smash them together. Suppose the heaviest two stones have weights x and y with x <= y. The result of this smash is: If x == y, both stones are destroyed, and If x != y, the stone of weight x is destroyed, and the stone of weight y has new weight y - x. At the end of the game, there is at most one stone left. Return the weight of the last remaining stone. If there are no stones left, return 0.

solutions.name: Sorting
solutions.explanation: Repeatedly sort array, pop two largest stones, compute difference, add back if non-zero. Continue until one or zero stones remain. Simple but inefficient due to repeated sorting on each iteration. O(n² log n) time complexity where n iterations each require O(n log n) sorting. Space O(1) or O(n) depending on sort implementation.

solutions.name: Heap
solutions.explanation: Use max-heap to efficiently get two largest stones. Python has min-heap, so negate values to simulate max-heap. Heapify initial array in O(n). Each iteration: pop two largest (O(log n)), compute difference, push back if non-zero (O(log n)). Process n stones with O(log n) operations. O(n log n) time complexity. Space O(n) for heap storage. Most efficient approach for this problem.

solutions.name: Bucket Sort
solutions.explanation: Use bucket array indexed by stone weight for counting. Find pairs of largest stones by scanning from max down. Track frequencies in bucket, handle pairs efficiently without explicit sorting. When odd count found at weight, find next available weight to pair with. Update frequencies accordingly. Optimal when max weight w is reasonable. O(n + w) time where w is max stone weight, O(w) space for bucket array.
